Gaming companies may offer a casino bonus that provides new potential customers with an increased value proposition as an incentive for them to sign up.
Absolutely not, they can vary within gaming companies and between gaming companies. Within each gaming company, there could be one standard bonus, or several available bonuses depending on the amount of money you deposit or the kinds of games that will be played.
For example, for table games, there might be a standard 100% matching of your deposit up to $200. However, if you know you will be depositing more than $200, there could be another level of bonus, matching your deposit at a lower rate, say 50%, but up to a higher bonus amount in currency value, like $1,000. This kind of bonus is usually termed a ‘VIP’ bonus or ‘high-roller’ bonus.
Also within the same online casino, if you like slots, there might be a separate standard bonus, specific to slots, with a higher available bonus amount compared to table games.
Between casino sites, bonuses can be defined in different ways. Some casinos promote their bonuses separately; one for slots, another for table games. Some casinos promote the sum total bonus amount for slots and table games together. In this case, the figure can look impressive, but if you only care about certain kinds of games, you may only be able to take advantage of the part of the bonus that is applicable to your games of interest. This is further evidence for why you need to read the bonus terms and conditions.
All bonus offer headlines are short by nature in order to get your attention. They usually include a currency amount, or it might use the term ‘free’ or ‘deposit bonus.’ Rest assured, no offer from an online casino truly offers free money, so be sure to spend a few minutes reading the offer terms and conditions. The most reputable companies create bonuses with very simple terms, rather than those that might be long or overly confusing.
All gaming companies stipulate what you must do in their terms and conditions in order to receive the value offered in their bonus. Most often, it will require that you make a minimum deposit into your account. Then, they will likely define the thresholds that need to be met in terms of how much you must play with or ‘roll over’ your deposited funds before your bonus might be attributed to your account, and when the bonus funds might be eligible for withdrawal as money.
In other words, do not sign up for a casino bonus thinking you can game the system. The terms and conditions are set so that new players might be able to enjoy extra credits in their account toward enjoying more casino play. The bonuses are not meant to be for free cash that can be withdrawn right away. Know what you are signing up for, read your bonus offer terms and conditions carefully.
Note that if you are particularly interested in a certain kind of casino game, you should look to read how that game might be handled with regard to the wagering requirements. Does playing your preferred game actually count toward your wagering requirements? If you love slots, it is more than likely that your wagering requirements will include slots play at a 1 to 1 rate. However, if you like certain table games like Blackjack, Roulette, Baccarat or others, the associated wagering requirements might be higher compared to slots games. For some casino bonuses, play within the live dealer casino games might not be included for your offer at all. These are the kinds of things that you should be looking for in the offer terms if you have very specific gaming tastes or preferences.
In other words, make sure that your casino bonus will actually apply for the games you really want to play by reading the T&C. It only takes two to three minutes to make this quick check.

Online casinos must submit to regular testing of their random number generators to ensure their games yield fair payouts. In these certificates, you will find that fairness is expressed through ‘RTP’, or the percentage of money that is ‘Returned To Player.’ Although RTP can be broken down by all the different games offered at a casino, the aggregate RTP for OddsJet online casinos tends to be 96% or higher. This means that 96 cents out of every Dollar, Euro or Pound that is played, is returned to players through winnings. RTP is used to reflect a general level of fairness for the casino as a whole over the course of many, many plays. It is not meant to be used with regard to the experience of an individual player.
To put this 96% RTP figure into context, it helps to compare it to real world gaming jurisdictions. If you were to visit a casino in Las Vegas, by Nevada law, a minimum of 75% RTP is required. If you were to play a ‘fruit machine’ in a Casino in Britain, their law states a minimum RTP of 70%. In Australia, machines must have a minimum RTP of 85% to 90% depending on their location. Thus in comparison, online casinos tend to return money to players at a much fairer rate.
In Ontario, the law mandates that each real slot machine must have an RTP of at least 85%, which is considerably lower than our listed online casinos. You can find this information at the OLG PlaySmart odds explanation. When you check out the PlayNow online casino in BC, they don't even display a random number generation audit of their RTP figures. All the online casinos that we list must submit to regular testing of their service to uphold their licenses in the various jurisdictions, which include these figures.
As the various provincial governments have hold a defacto monopoly on 'legal' gambling, they are obliged to use uncompetitive RTP rates. As shown above in BC, they don't even feel compelled to share information on the level of fairness under which they operate. As such, you will generally get a more fair experience through our listed online casinos for Canadians, where RTP generally exceeds 95% in aggregate, and often much higher for particular game types. Remember, RTP will not apply to your individual experience, but rather it is an indication of the overall fairness levels of their gaming experience as tested over millions of plays.
